items.title: 玖年 AI 日报 2026-11-10 🔥
items.summary:
玖年 AI 日报 2026-11-10 🔥

1. @Google Google于11月10日把Carbon开放给付费API开发者和企业，并向Ultra订阅者推出。尝鲜价每百万输入token 2美元、输出10美元，Antigravity的/swarm仍是预览。这次增量是准入扩大，不是首次出现；Carbon可能消耗更多token，单价相同不等于整任务同价，网络安全专用途径仍走Fairwind。

2. @claudeai 11月10日Claude Whiteboards和Sheets推出beta，Dashboards转正并更名Data，面向付费计划。表格支持公式与导出，Data可提供经批准查询的实时结果。Sheets仍是基础表格功能；Enterprise白板和表格默认关闭，Data计划11月19日默认开启。共享结果不等于给查看者底层数据权限。

3. @OpenAI OpenAI推出Businesses beta，商家验证后可维护资料、价格和库存，并查看达到门槛的汇总提及与点击数据。Business Agent先面向美国符合条件的电商和在线服务企业。商家不获得用户对话；Agent会话和赞助展示有单独标识，不能把商家Agent当成ChatGPT独立回答，也不是全球所有企业都可开通Agent。

4. @Google Google与Artificial Analysis发布MKA：200项任务覆盖10个行业、83种职业，评分兼顾事实与视觉设计。模型使用同一Stirrup harness、工具和回合预算。200项评测集保持私有，另公开10个样例；自动评分与专家96%一致不是模型96%正确。本轮仅回读方法博客，未完整审阅技术报告或复现。

5. @Google Google在11月10日的Pixel Drop公告中称Gemini Intelligence已到Pixel 10，并加入自定义小组件、改进搜索和Gemini增强的来电筛选。Pixel Tag从次日开始接受订购。公告列出多种设备能力，不代表旧Pixel同时获得全部功能；本轮没有操作手机、验证地区覆盖或测试实际效果，也不把可订购写成已经交付。

6. @OpenAINewsroom OpenAI将于12月11日退役ChatGPT Voice中的Advanced和Standard语音模式，集中改进GPT-Live。官方同时说明，实时视频和屏幕共享仍由Advanced voice支撑，直到GPT-Live具备相应能力。这是未来迁移公告，不是今天停用全部语音；视频与屏幕共享存在明确过渡例外，不能省略。本轮不播放或评价语音样本。

7. @cursor_ai Cursor于11月10日重构Projects，提供共享任务板、团队上下文和跨成员agent通信；每人仍有自身agent与本地上下文。功能以beta向全部用户逐步推出。共享层可以帮助交接与发现工作重叠，但官方案例不证明冲突已被普遍消除；逐步推出也不等于每个账号此刻都已获得功能。

8. @pytorch PyTorch在11月10日介绍ExecuTorch WebGPU后端：模型导出为.pte后可在支持WebGPU的浏览器内使用GPU运行，不必转换成其他框架格式。后端覆盖文字、视觉和语音等已验证模型。后端仍处早期开发；速度比较基于M1 Pro、Chrome和指定小模型，不能推成所有设备提升。本轮未运行Playground，也不把端侧推理等同整站绝无遥测。

9. @OpenRouter 本轮新读OpenRouter的MCP、CLI与Skills对照：同一个GitHub任务中，Sonnet的CLI输入1421token，默认46工具MCP为59417。缩窄工具并只返回所需字段可明显降耗。实验在10月20日、每组仅三次，文章标注11月11日；这是新公开分析而非今日重测。Tool Search因模型和错误重试而异，不能断言MCP总比CLI差。

10. @pydantic Pydantic在11月10日解释，code mode用程序编排工具、减少模型往返；沙箱决定代码在哪运行、能接触什么。隔离模型写的程序，与隔离工具执行，是不同边界。Monty里的代码受限，但外部工具仍可能携带宿主权限；LocalWorkspace也不是沙箱。文章是方法说明，本轮没有安装或改变本机执行权限。

items.title: The AI Race is Putting Patients at Risk - Progressive.org
items.summary: Indeed, the most frightening risks involving AI are already moving from theory to capability. Frontier models let non-experts code new applications quickly, and soon it may be possible to use AI to create biological agents that can be weaponized. The White House’s own AI Action Plan warns that AI could create new pathways for bad actors to synthesize dangerous pathogens and calls for stronger screening and national security assessment of AI tools and systems. Anthropic has already said its [...] AI in health care offers many cases that regulatory frameworks should be addressing. A hospital can use AI for patient care and clinical decision support; an insurer for utilization management (e.g., automating care denials); a teenager for mental health advice; a public health department for outbreak detection; and a bad actor for infiltrating a hospital network. Different uses carry different risks and require separate risk-benefit analysis for determining regulatory guardrails. [...] Japan created an AI Strategy Headquarters headed by the prime minister and adopted a national AI basic plan. The United Kingdom and Australia are linking their AI safety institutes in order to better evaluate frontier AI model risks. These systems differ, but they have one thing in common - national AI governance.

items.title: AI Has Entered the Boardroom. Who’s Overseeing It? | Stanford Graduate School of Business
items.summary:
In the survey, 75% of directors said they used AI for research and market analysis, 55% for board prep and material summarization. Other common uses included strategic question generation and competitive benchmarking. Matthys says that board members would ideally like to use AI “to track and summarize board packages and more quickly understand year-to-year trends by using LLM tools rather than reading 80- to 100-page reports.” [...] The sooner the better, the researchers suggest. “Moving too slowly with AI governance means you may miss out on opportunities,” Saripalli says. “The board has fiduciary responsibility for anything that has impact at the product or service level.”

“The risk of not moving is as serious as the risk of AI systems running amok,” Matthys adds, noting how past technological shifts have left unprepared companies behind. “If you don’t keep up, there’s a risk that 20 years from now you won’t exist.” [...] ## In Brief

 A new survey finds that corporate boards are not keeping up with AI governance.
 Directors report that they are discussing and using AI, yet their boards lack a systematic approach to oversight.
 Companies that wait to define AI strategy and audit their AI use risk being left behind.

“We’re trying to change the wheels on the bus while driving it at 100 miles an hour downhill.”

“Generative AI quickly gained a negative reputation because it was seen as a tool for cheating,” she said. “That misses the point. STUDENTS PUT AI TO WORK [...] To address bias in clinical decision-making tools, Wang founded the Healthcare AI Initiative (HAI) at Chapman, bringing together researchers working on pressing healthcare challenges. HAI examines ethical questions surrounding AI, including data privacy, and develops equitable machine learning approaches.

items.title: Hochul cites Democratic control of Congress in pushing AI regulation, federal dollars

She’s likely to lean on Schumer and Jeffries, who are angling for leadership positions. Jeffries stumped for her on the eve of Election Day.

Though there are dozens of competing AI-enforcement bills currently floating around Capitol Hill, the governor says Congress should adopt New York’s Responsible AI Safety and Education Act.

The law takes effect on Jan. 1 and is set to force big AI companies to publish specific safety protocols — or else face civil penalties. [...] Hochul says she will use her relationships with New York Democrats in Washington to speed up artificial intelligence regulations — a sharp contrast from a lack thereof under the current congressional makeup and roadblocks by the Trump administration.

“When they start looking for ways to regulate AI, the first place they should look is New York. Because we are building a national model for smart, sensible AI regulation,” Hochul said. [...] So far, the Hochul administration says at least two companies have agreed to sign on, but declined to say which ones.

“We evolve as the threats grow bigger and bigger. We were concerned about social media and the addictive algorithms on children two years ago,” Hochul said.

“Now, we have to do something even more dramatic than we had done last year with signing the RAISE ACT. Unfortunately, we’re in a place of ‘catch up all the time,’” she added.

items.summary: These days, resistance to tech is typically framed in terms of individual choices: if we buy the Brick, limit our children’s screen time, delete the worst apps from our phones, stop doomscrolling, and refuse to use ChatGPT for anything other than the most mundane searches, we will be released from the grasp of Big Tech. Freedom becomes a question of your own will power. In 2022, the Times published a charming story about “Luddite” teens in Brooklyn who met up in Prospect Park once a week to [...] I have been thinking and writing about resistance to technology for a while, spurred by an unresolved alarm that Americans have not put up much of a fight against the sense of alienation caused by our growing dependence on screens. It’s increasingly clear to me that we will not survive as a society without some seismic intervention that separates us from our screens, our algorithms, and our little simulacra of social life. I believe that such a rupture will come—but what will it look like? A hospital can use AI for patient care and clinical decision support; an insurer for utilization management (e.g., automating care denials); a teenager for mental health advice; a public health department for outbreak detection; and a bad actor for infiltrating a hospital network. Different uses carry different risks and require separate risk-benefit analysis for determining regulatory guardrails. results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

result.actual_text:
```python
def fibonacci(n: int) -> int:
    """
    Tính số Fibonacci thứ n bằng cách sử dụng đệ quy.

    Parameters
    ----------
    n : int
        Chỉ số của dãy Fibonacci (n >= 0).

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Giá trị của số Fibonacci thứ n.

    Notes
    -----
    - Fibonacci(0) = 0
    - Fibonacci(1) = 1
    - Đệ quy có độ phức tạp lũy thừa, nên không thích hợp cho n lớn.
    """
    if n < 0:
        raise ValueError("n phải là số nguyên không âm")
    if n == 0:
        return 0
    if n == 1:
        return 1
    return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)
```

Bạn có thể thử chạy:

```python
print(fibonacci(10))  # Output: 55
```

> **Lưu ý**: Đệ quy truyền thống sẽ rất chậm khi `n` lớn (ví dụ `n > 30`). Để tính nhanh hơn, bạn có thể dùng memoization hoặc phương pháp vòng lặp.

Articulated robots: Multi-axis robotic arms used for welding, painting, assembly, and heavy material handling. They remain particularly relevant to automotive production.

Historically, manufacturers deployed robots primarily for repetitive, high-volume operations, including welding vehicle bodies, painting components, and transferring materials between production stations. A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.
